title: Transport a relation through an explicit conversion
obstacle: The input and target use different representations of the same intended objects.
procedure: State the source and destination types and the conversion explicitly.
Prove that this conversion preserves the particular relation needed by the target.
Apply the resulting bridge or congruence lemma at the exact target type.
verification: Check the bridge and its application in Lean; verify that no converse or injectivity was assumed.
positive_example: Transport an equality through a specified function using congruence.
negative_example: Infer equality of original objects from equal images without injectivity.

evidence.note: Editorially generalized guidance under this maintenance policy; no independent effectiveness result or proof acceptance is claimed.

title: Distinguish quotient objects from their representatives
obstacle: A statement about equivalence classes is being used as a statement about chosen representatives.
procedure: Identify which statements concern classes and which concern representatives.
Prove invariance before descending a construction, or supply the additional hypotheses needed to choose and compare representatives.
Keep class equality and representative equality as separate typed claims.
verification: Lean-check the descended construction or representative bridge with all invariance or uniqueness hypotheses explicit.
positive_example: Descend a function after proving it has equal values on equivalent inputs.
negative_example: Evaluate an arbitrary representative-dependent function on a quotient class.

evidence.note: Editorially generalized guidance under this maintenance policy; no independent effectiveness result or proof acceptance is claimed.

title: Isolate changes of convention in a reusable bridge
obstacle: Two definitions express related constructions under different conventions.
procedure: Write the definitions and the proposed map between their data.
Prove the required identity with every scale, sign, ordering and domain condition explicit.
Reuse that typed identity in the main proof instead of treating conventions as definitionally equal.
verification: Compile the bridge and compare both endpoints with the stated definitions.
positive_example: Prove a conversion between two explicit coordinate conventions.
negative_example: Replace one convention by another based only on similar notation.

evidence.note: Editorially generalized guidance under this maintenance policy; no independent effectiveness result or proof acceptance is claimed.

title: Expose a suitable algebraic form before automation
obstacle: Arithmetic automation cannot match the current expression to its supported form.
procedure: Prove required side conditions such as signs or nonzero denominators.
Unfold only wrappers that obstruct the intended algebraic representation.
Resolve casts explicitly, normalize the expression, and use automation on the resulting algebraic goal.
verification: Compile the normalized equality or inequality under the original assumptions.
positive_example: Normalize a polynomial identity after aligning coefficient types.
negative_example: Cancel a denominator without establishing that it is nonzero.

evidence.note: Editorially generalized guidance under this maintenance policy; no independent effectiveness result or proof acceptance is claimed.

title: Separate approximation from passage to a limit
obstacle: An infinite construction is easier to compare on finite or otherwise controlled approximants.
procedure: Prove the needed relation for the approximants.
Establish convergence in the topology required by the chosen operation.
Use an applicable continuity or limit theorem with its hypotheses proved, then identify the limit.
verification: Check the approximating relation, convergence hypotheses and exact limit theorem separately in Lean.
positive_example: Pass a proved relation through a continuous map after proving convergence.
negative_example: Commute an arbitrary operation with a limit from pointwise convergence alone.

evidence.note: Editorially generalized guidance under this maintenance policy; no independent effectiveness result or proof acceptance is claimed.

title: Prove domain and side conditions before applying a partial construction
obstacle: A function or theorem is available only for data satisfying a specified domain condition.
procedure: Read the complete domain and hypotheses of the intended application.
Prove membership and other required conditions from the current permitted inputs.
Apply the construction to the qualified data and retain the condition in later interface transfers.
verification: Compile the exact application without introducing additional assumptions.
positive_example: Construct an element of a subtype only after proving its predicate.
negative_example: Treat a partially defined construction as applicable to arbitrary data.

evidence.note: Editorially generalized guidance under this maintenance policy; no independent effectiveness result or proof acceptance is claimed.

title: Preserve quantifier order when strengthening convergence
obstacle: A pointwise statement is being used to support a conclusion uniform over a family.
procedure: Write the pointwise and uniform quantifiers side by side.
Identify and prove the additional control needed for one choice to serve the whole family.
Only use the uniform statement after proving it in the target topology.
verification: Check that the final witness or threshold has exactly the permitted parameter dependencies.
positive_example: Prove a single threshold works for every member of a finite family.
negative_example: Move a threshold outside a universal quantifier when it still depends on that variable.

evidence.note: Editorially generalized guidance under this maintenance policy; no independent effectiveness result or proof acceptance is claimed.

title: Track witness and constant dependencies before specialization
obstacle: A chosen witness or constant may depend on data that the target requires it to be independent of.
procedure: Record the order in which parameters and witnesses are chosen.
Prove the quantified statement before substituting special values.
Inspect each specialization and the exported signature for additional dependencies.
verification: Compare the complete binder order and dependency graph with the target.
positive_example: Choose a witness after the variables on which it is allowed to depend.
negative_example: Promote a family of parameter-dependent constants to one universal constant.

evidence.note: Editorially generalized guidance under this maintenance policy; no independent effectiveness result or proof acceptance is claimed.

title: Keep external statements faithful and derive local consequences internally
obstacle: A cited result is being packaged into a formal premise for a different setting.
procedure: Restate every source hypothesis, quantifier and conclusion field.
Compare the typed external premise with that statement.
Prove specialization and representation bridges internally from permitted inputs.
verification: Check source correspondence and each bridge separately; compilation alone does not verify attribution.
positive_example: Instantiate a verified universal source theorem at admissible data.
negative_example: Add the desired application result as an unmentioned field of the external premise.

evidence.note: Editorially generalized guidance under this maintenance policy; no independent effectiveness result or proof acceptance is claimed.

title: Prove reindexing before transferring an aggregate
obstacle: A sum, supremum or other indexed construction is being expressed using a different index type.
procedure: State the index map and the exact coverage or multiplicity needed.
Prove the term correspondence and handle empty or exceptional indices.
Apply the aggregate reindexing theorem with its convergence or order hypotheses.
verification: Compile the aggregate identity and inspect its endpoint and convergence conventions.
positive_example: Reindex a finite sum through a proved bijection.
negative_example: Drop repeated or missing terms while claiming an unchanged aggregate.

evidence.note: Editorially generalized guidance under this maintenance policy; no independent effectiveness result or proof acceptance is claimed.

title: Verify the actual exported theorem signature
obstacle: A convenient wrapper may hide extra premises or omit part of the requested conclusion.
procedure: Inspect the actual exported declaration, including implicit and structure-valued arguments.
Expand the proposition fields needed to compare it with the full target.
Derive necessary prerequisites from allowed inputs and assemble the intended theorem.
verification: Check the exported signature against every target hypothesis and conclusion, then inspect its trust dependencies.
positive_example: Derive an intermediate prerequisite inside the theorem from existing hypotheses.
negative_example: Expose that prerequisite as a new assumption of the exported theorem.

evidence.note: Editorially generalized guidance under this maintenance policy; no independent effectiveness result or proof acceptance is claimed.

title: Freeze conditional interfaces before parallel proof construction
obstacle: Independent proof bodies must be assembled without relying on hidden state.
procedure: Freeze shared definitions and each typed input and output.
Provide each proof task its conditional goal and complete permitted direct inputs.
Check the bodies independently, substitute actual upstream proofs, and recheck the assembled theorem.
verification: Compile the complete assembled artifact; local conditional checks alone are insufficient.
positive_example: Implement independent conditional bodies with unchanged signatures.
negative_example: Change a producer signature while consumers still use a previously frozen version.

evidence.note: Editorially generalized guidance under this maintenance policy; no independent effectiveness result or proof acceptance is claimed.

title: Inspect the pinned library signature before integration
obstacle: A remembered library call does not match its actual type or required instances.
procedure: Search the pinned source for the needed statement shape.
Read the full type, parameters and instances; check a minimal application in the intended context.
Supply difficult parameters explicitly and integrate the checked application into the larger proof.
verification: Compile the application under the actual project pins and retain the observed type.
positive_example: Check an implicit parameter explicitly before integrating a library call.
negative_example: Guess an argument order from a theorem name or a different library version.

evidence.note: Editorially generalized guidance under this maintenance policy; no independent effectiveness result or proof acceptance is claimed.

title: Separate execution health from proof outcome
obstacle: A run ended or stalled without enough evidence to identify the failed layer.
procedure: Inspect the actual tool, transport and controller result for the failed operation.
Record task outcome separately from execution health, including unknowns.
Apply the configured recovery policy only to positively identified recoverable faults.
verification: Tie the stated fault to recorded evidence; elapsed time alone does not establish either a proof gap or healthy search.
positive_example: Report a provider error separately from an unfinished proof.
negative_example: Call a transport failure a mathematical rejection or claim a timeout when no limit existed.

evidence.note: Editorially generalized guidance under this maintenance policy; no independent effectiveness result or proof acceptance is claimed.

title: Export every fact needed by a downstream proof
obstacle: A downstream proof requires a formula that appears only inside a producer proof body.
procedure: Identify the exact downstream formula, binders and conditions.
If absent from the public interface, revise the source and obtain the required review of the changed boundary.
Regenerate dependent packets and typed interfaces; use only the exported fact.
verification: Replay the consumer from its declared direct inputs without consulting producer bodies.
positive_example: Export a proved intermediate identity with its hypotheses before using it elsewhere.
negative_example: Import a formula remembered from a producer proof that is absent from its output.

evidence.note: Editorially generalized guidance under this maintenance policy; no independent effectiveness result or proof acceptance is claimed.

title: Localize native timeouts before expanding proof search
obstacle: A recorded native Lean resource limit prevents a candidate from returning useful proof feedback.
procedure: Read the actual native result and confirm owned-process cleanup. Distinguish wall timeout, heartbeat exhaustion, definitional-equality work and an earlier ordinary error from provider or controller faults.
Preserve the candidate, exact target, declared premises, imports, versions and resource settings before changing its implementation. Do not treat a timeout as a mathematical rejection.

Locate the costly application or tactic using a bounded local fragment or retained diagnostics. Address the earliest ordinary type error before interpreting later resource errors; a very small diagnostic allowance may also reject valid code.

For expensive implicit inference, inspect the full declaration type and supply the function, object, exponent, index and coercion types explicitly where needed. Name typed intermediate facts rather than asking unification to reconstruct a nested expression.

For an equality or representation bridge, state the intermediate function and the required equality direction explicitly. Use a small checked change, convert, congrArg or extensionality step and a restricted simp only list instead of broad unfolding.

For broad closure or recursive automation, construct intermediate closure facts from the leaves and compose the specific lemmas explicitly. Do not replace every use of automation without locating its cost.

Recheck the smallest changed application with a finite allowance, then the complete original target with all its original inputs. Retain unsuccessful candidates and diagnostics; a faster fragment alone does not establish complete acceptance.

If the selected branch does not help, revisit the diagnosis rather than blindly repeating it or raising limits. Changes to mathematical boundaries require the normal reviewed source/interface procedure.
verification: The repaired complete candidate must pass a fresh native check under the pinned environment with the unchanged target and premises; compare performance only with disclosed comparable settings, and keep mathematical audits separate.
positive_example: A native equality-check timeout is addressed by a typed intermediate function and a short checked equality bridge, followed by a complete candidate recheck.
negative_example: Delete an equality reversal, replace every tactic or increase every timeout solely because an unrelated candidate once compiled afterward.

evidence.note: Bounded retrospective comparisons of completed implementations motivate this diagnostic procedure; individual edits were not all causally isolated and broader effectiveness is unestablished.
